Anton von Werner was a German painter born in Frankfurt an der Oder in 1843. He lived in Berlin, where he became director of the art academy and the leading painter of the Prussian court, recording events such as the proclamation of the German Empire. He died in Berlin in 1915.

Lucas Cranach the Elder was a German painter born in Kronach in 1472. He became court painter to the rulers of Saxony in Wittenberg, was a close friend of Martin Luther, and ran a busy workshop that made portraits, religious scenes and the first Protestant images. He died in Weimar in 1553.
x-ferdinand-pauwels-attributed

Ferdinand Pauwels was a Belgian painter born in Eeklo in 1830. He became a professor at the art academy in Dresden, Germany, and painted large scenes from the history of the Reformation. This picture is attributed to him, which means experts think but cannot prove that he painted it. He died in Dresden in 1904.

Albrecht Dürer was a German artist born in Nuremberg in 1471. He was a painter, but he is most famous for his woodcuts and engravings, which made him known across Europe, and for traveling to Italy to learn from Renaissance artists. He lived mostly in Nuremberg and died there in 1528.

Gerlach Flicke was a German painter born in Osnabrück around 1495. He moved to England, where he lived in London and painted portraits, including one of Archbishop Thomas Cranmer. He died in London in 1558.
x-british-school

This painting is by an unknown English artist working in the 1540s. Many English paintings of the time were made by artists whose names have not survived, and later experts label them with the name 'British School' or 'English School'.

Pasquale Cati was an Italian painter born in Jesi in about 1550. He worked in Rome, where he painted frescoes and altarpieces for churches in the style of the Catholic Counter-Reformation. He died there in 1620.

Daniel Maclise was an Irish painter born in Cork in 1806. He moved to London, where he painted big scenes from history and literature, including huge murals in the Houses of Parliament, and was close friends with Charles Dickens. He died in Chelsea in 1870.

Titian was an Italian painter born in Pieve di Cadore around 1490. He worked in Venice and became the most famous painter in Europe, painting portraits for the Emperor Charles V and King Philip II of Spain with rich color and loose brushwork. He lived to a great age and died in Venice in 1576.
x-english-school-formerly-attributed-to-ge

The Armada Portrait was painted by an unknown English artist in 1588. It was once thought to be by George Gower, Queen Elizabeth's Serjeant-Painter, but experts now believe it came from a workshop of several painters, and it exists in a few versions.
x-english-school
This painting was made by an unknown English artist around 1590. Many paintings of the Armada were made soon after the battle, and the painters of these often did not sign their works.
x-english-school-attributed-to-marcus-ghee

The Rainbow Portrait of Elizabeth I was painted by an unknown English artist around 1602. It is sometimes attributed to Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger, a leading court portrait painter of the time, but experts are not sure.
x-attributed-to-robert-peake-the-elder

Robert Peake the Elder was an English painter born around 1551 who worked in London. He was the Serjeant-Painter to King James I and painted portraits of the court, including the royal family, in a bright, detailed style. He died in London in 1619.

Antonis Mor was a Dutch painter born in Utrecht in about 1517. He became the court portrait painter to the Habsburgs and painted Philip II of Spain and Queen Mary I of England, working in Brussels, Madrid and London. He died in Antwerp in about 1577.
x-unknown-artist
The artist of this work is not known. Many early portraits, prints and manuscripts were made by artists whose names were never recorded or have since been lost.

John de Critz was a painter born in Antwerp around 1551 who moved to London as a boy. He became Serjeant-Painter to King James I, painting portraits and decorating royal buildings. He lived in London until he died in 1642.

Robert Herdman was a Scottish painter born in Rattray in Perthshire in 1829. He lived in Edinburgh and painted scenes from Scottish history and everyday life, and became a leading member of the Royal Scottish Academy. He died in Edinburgh in 1888.

Diego Velázquez was a Spanish painter born in Seville in 1599. He moved to Madrid as a young man and became the court painter to King Philip IV, painting portraits such as Las Meninas that are among the greatest in the world. He died in Madrid in 1660.

Gerard ter Borch was a Dutch painter born in Zwolle in 1617. He traveled widely, including to Münster where he painted the signing of the treaty of 1648, and was famous for quiet indoor scenes with beautifully painted satin dresses. He lived in Deventer and died there in 1681.

Peter Snayers was a Flemish painter born in Antwerp in 1592. He became the court painter to the Archduke in Brussels and was famous for his panoramic battle scenes, often showing real battles of the Thirty Years' War. He died in Brussels in 1667.

Václav Brožík was a Czech painter born in Trhová Kamenice in 1851. He studied in Prague, Dresden and Munich, and moved to Paris, where he painted big scenes from Czech and European history. He died in Paris in 1901.
x-workshop-of-matthaus-merian

Matthäus Merian was a Swiss-born engraver who lived in Frankfurt, Germany, and published famous books of city views and the news of the Thirty Years' War. This engraving is from his workshop, which kept making prints after he died in 1650.

Bartholomeus van der Helst was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1613. He moved to Amsterdam, where he became one of the most successful portrait painters of his time, rivaling Rembrandt. He died in Amsterdam in 1670.

Dirck van Delen was a Dutch painter born in Heusden in 1605. He specialized in imaginary views of church and palace interiors, and lived for most of his life in Arnemuiden and Middelburg in Zeeland. He died in Middelburg in 1671.

Hendrick Cornelisz Vroom was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1562. He is often called the father of Dutch marine painting, and made pictures of ships and sea battles for admirals and the government. He lived in Haarlem and died there in 1640.

Reinier Nooms, also called Zeeman, was a Dutch painter and etcher born in Amsterdam around 1623. He had been a sailor, and he made detailed pictures of ships, harbors and sea battles. He died in Amsterdam in 1664.
x-henri-ambrosius-pacx
Henri Ambrosius Pacx was a painter who made a picture of Prince Maurice of Orange at the Battle of Nieuwpoort in the 1800s, long after the battle itself. Very little is known about his life.

Karl Friedrich Lessing was a German painter born in Breslau in 1808. He worked in Düsseldorf, where he painted dramatic scenes from the Reformation and medieval history, and later directed the art gallery in Karlsruhe. He died in Karlsruhe in 1880.

Eduard Steinbrück was a German painter born in Magdeburg in 1802. He worked in Berlin and Düsseldorf and painted historical and religious scenes and portraits. He died in Lądek-Zdrój, now in Poland, in 1882.

Jennie Augusta Brownscombe was an American painter born in Honesdale, Pennsylvania, in 1850. She became famous for her warm pictures of American history, especially the Pilgrims and Thanksgiving, and she lived and worked in New York. She died in Queens in 1936.

Henry Bacon was an American painter born in Haverhill, Massachusetts, in 1839. He fought in the Civil War, then lived in Paris for most of his life, painting scenes from American history and Egypt. He died in Cairo in 1912.

George Henry Boughton was a painter born in Norwich, England, in 1833, who was brought up in Albany, New York, and then lived in London. He painted gentle scenes of the Pilgrims and of early America and became a member of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1905.

William Halsall was an English-born American painter, born in Kirkdale near Liverpool in 1841. He moved to Boston and painted ships and the sea, including the Mayflower, and had a studio in the city. He died in Winthrop, Massachusetts, in 1919.

Jean Leon Gerome Ferris was an American painter born in Philadelphia in 1863. He painted a series of scenes of American history, from the Pilgrims to the Revolution, and his pictures were published in many schoolbooks. He died in Philadelphia in 1930.
Henry Brueckner was a painter who worked in the United States in the 1800s. He painted historical scenes, such as the marriage of Pocahontas, for patrons in the New World.

Pierre Gustave Staal was a French illustrator born in Vertus in 1817. He made lithographs and engravings of costumes and portraits, including a well-known portrait of Pocahontas, and lived in Paris, where he died in 1882.

Alonzo Chappel was an American painter and engraver born in New York City in 1828. He made hundreds of portraits and historical scenes of American history for books and prints. He lived and worked in New York and died in 1887.

Francis William Edmonds was an American painter born in Hudson, New York, in 1806. He was a banker who painted in his spare time, making charming scenes of everyday life. He lived in New York and died in Bronxville in 1863.
x-johannes-vingboons

Johannes Vingboons was a Dutch mapmaker and painter born in Amsterdam around 1616. He drew maps and views of the world for the Dutch West India Company, including early views of New Amsterdam, now New York. He lived in Amsterdam and died there around 1670.
Richard Rummell was an English-born American painter, born in 1848. He painted watercolor views of American college campuses and other buildings, and lived and worked in New York. He died in 1924.

Charles Landseer was an English painter born in London in 1799, the older brother of the animal painter Edwin Landseer. He painted historical scenes, especially from the English Civil War, and was the Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1879.
x-robert-walker

Robert Walker was an English portrait painter born around 1599 who worked in London. He painted many portraits of Oliver Cromwell and other leaders of the Parliamentary side in the English Civil War. He died in London around 1658.

William Frederick Yeames was an English painter born in Taganrog, Russia, in 1835, where his father was British consul. He moved to London and painted historical pictures, becoming a member of the Royal Academy. He died in Teignmouth in 1918.

John Michael Wright was a painter born in London in 1617, of Scottish descent. He lived in Rome as a young man and returned to England, where he painted portraits of King Charles II and his court. He died in London in 1694.

Jan van Huchtenburgh was a Dutch painter born in Haarlem in 1646. He specialized in battle scenes and made paintings for Prince Eugene of Savoy and King William III. He lived in Amsterdam and died there in 1733.

Andrew Carrick Gow was an English painter born in London in 1848. He painted battles and scenes from English history and became a member and later Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1920.

Alexander von Kotzebue was a Russian painter born in Königsberg in 1815, the son of the famous German dramatist. He became a battle painter for the Russian tsars and later lived in Munich. He died in Munich in 1889.

Alexey Bogolyubov was a Russian painter born in 1824 in the Novgorod region. He painted seas and ships, served as a painter for the Russian navy, and lived for many years in Paris, where he died in 1896.
Pierre-Denis Martin was a French painter born in Paris in 1663. He painted battle scenes, including some for the Russian court in the 1720s, and spent his life in Paris, where he died in 1742.

Godfrey Kneller was a German-born painter, born in Lübeck in 1646. He moved to England and became the most successful portrait painter in London, painting eight kings and queens as well as Isaac Newton. He died in London in 1723.

Alexey Venetsianov was a Russian painter born in Moscow in 1780. He is considered the founder of Russian paintings of peasant life, and started a school at his country estate. He died in 1847 in an accident when his horse bolted.

Anicet Charles Gabriel Lemonnier was a French painter born in Rouen in 1743. He worked in Paris and was the director of the royal Gobelins tapestry works. He painted the Salon of Madame Geoffrin and died in Paris in 1824.

Joseph-Siffred Duplessis was a French painter born in Carpentras in 1725. He became one of the best portrait painters in Paris, painting Louis XVI and the American Benjamin Franklin, and he was the curator of the royal paintings at Versailles. He died there in 1802.

Charles-Nicolas Cochin was a French engraver and draftsman born in Paris in 1715. He was an official artist for Louis XV and the keeper of drawings at the Louvre, and he drew the frontispiece of the Encyclopédie. He died in Paris in 1790.

Dmitry Levitzky was a Russian painter born in Kyiv in 1735. He became the leading portrait painter in Saint Petersburg during the reign of Catherine the Great, painting nobles and thinkers, including Diderot. He died in Saint Petersburg in 1822.
Sébastien Leclerc was a French engraver born in Metz in 1637. He worked in Paris for Louis XIV, making many prints of the king's science and military projects. He died in Paris in 1714.

Friedrich Georg Weitsch was a German painter born in Brunswick in 1758. He worked in Berlin as a painter for the Prussian court and painted many portraits, including one of the scientist Alexander von Humboldt. He died in Berlin in 1828.

Thomas Davies was a British army officer and artist born in Shooter's Hill, near London, in 1737. He served in Canada and the American colonies and made watercolors of what he saw, which are some of the earliest views of North America. He died in Blackheath in 1812.
Louis Bombled was a French painter and illustrator born in Chantilly in 1862. He specialized in military subjects and painted battle scenes for books and magazines. He died in Pierrefonds in 1927.

Francis Hayman was an English painter born in Exeter in 1708. He worked in London, painting scenes for the pleasure gardens at Vauxhall and large history pictures, and was one of the founders of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1776.
x-anonymous-artist
This work was made by an artist whose name was not recorded. Many historical paintings and prints, especially from the time of the events themselves, were made by anonymous artists.
Pierre-Charles Canot was a French engraver born around 1710 who moved to London. He engraved many sea scenes and battle pictures, and died in London in 1777.

John Henry Walker was an Irish-born illustrator, born in County Antrim in 1831, who moved to Canada. He lived in Montreal, where he drew historical and city scenes for books and newspapers, and he died there in 1899.

Hervey Smythe was a British army officer born in 1734. He served under General Wolfe at Quebec in 1759 and made drawings of the campaign, then served as an adviser on military matters. He died in 1811.

John Ward Dunsmore was an American painter born in Ohio in 1856. He studied in Paris and became known for paintings of events of the American Revolution, which were used in schoolbooks. He died in 1945.
x-paul-revere

Paul Revere was born in Boston in 1735 and became a silversmith, engraver and patriot. He is best known for his midnight ride in April 1775 to warn colonists that British soldiers were coming. He made the engraving of the Boston Massacre, and died in Boston in 1818.

William Ranney was an American painter born in Middletown, Connecticut, in 1813. He fought in the Texas Revolution as a young man and painted scenes of the American West and of the Revolutionary War. He lived in New Jersey and died in West Hoboken in 1857.

Rembrandt Peale was an American painter born in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, in 1778, the son of the painter Charles Willson Peale. He painted portraits of Thomas Jefferson and George Washington, and lived in Philadelphia, where he died in 1860.

Thomas Sully was an English-born American painter born in Horncastle in 1783. He moved to America as a boy, settled in Philadelphia and painted portraits of many leaders, including Queen Victoria. He died in Philadelphia in 1872.
Horace Vernet was a French painter born in Paris in 1789. He painted many battles of Napoleon and the French army, and lived in Rome and Paris, where he died in 1863.

Isidore Stanislas Helman was a French engraver born in Lille in 1743. He moved to Paris, where he engraved scenes of the French Revolution after the paintings of other artists, and his prints were widely sold.

Jean Duplessis-Bertaux was a French engraver and painter born in Paris in 1747. He is known for his lively prints of the events of the French Revolution and the Napoleonic wars. He lived in Paris and died there in 1818.

Thomas Falcon Marshall was an English painter born in Liverpool in 1818. He lived in London and painted historical and storytelling pictures, many of them about the English Civil War and Mary Queen of Scots. He died in Kensington in 1878.

Jacques Bertaux was a French painter born in Harcy in the 1740s. He worked in Paris, and is best remembered for a vivid painting of the storming of the Tuileries Palace on August 10, 1792, which he made while the events were fresh.

Reinier Vinkeles was a Dutch engraver and draftsman born in Amsterdam in 1741. He made prints of history and portraits, including scenes of the French Revolution for Dutch audiences. He lived in Amsterdam and died there in 1816.

Adolph Northen was a German painter born in Hann. Münden in 1828. He studied in Düsseldorf and became known for dramatic paintings of Napoleon's campaigns in Russia and of Prussian history. He died in Düsseldorf in 1876.

François Gérard was a French painter born in Rome in 1770. He studied under Jacques-Louis David, became a favorite portrait painter of Napoleon's court, and was later made a baron. He lived in Paris and died there in 1837.

Henri Félix Emmanuel Philippoteaux was a French painter born in Paris in 1815. He made large battle paintings and giant circular panoramas, including a famous one of Gettysburg. He died in Paris in 1884.

Peter von Hess was a German painter born in Düsseldorf in 1792. He worked in Munich and became the leading battle painter of Bavaria, painting scenes of the Napoleonic wars and the Greek War of Independence. He died in Munich in 1871.

Thomas Lawrence was an English painter born in Bristol in 1769. He became the most fashionable portrait painter of his time, painting kings, generals and beautiful ladies, and was president of the Royal Academy. He lived in London and died there in 1830.

Carl Blechen was a German painter born in Cottbus in 1798. He lived in Berlin, traveled to Italy, and painted romantic landscapes and some of the earliest pictures of factories and industry in German art. He died in Berlin in 1840.

David Roberts was a Scottish painter born in Stockbridge, Edinburgh, in 1796. He started as a theater scene painter, traveled through Egypt and the Holy Land, and made famous views of ancient monuments. He lived in London and died there in 1864.
James Pollard was an English painter born in London in 1792. He specialized in lively pictures of stagecoaches, inns and early railways, and he lived in London, where he died in 1867.

Henry Courtney Selous was an English painter and illustrator born in Deptford in 1803. He painted big historical pictures and illustrated books, including a famous painting of the opening of the Great Exhibition in 1851. He died in Devon in 1890.

Constantin Meunier was a Belgian sculptor and painter born in Etterbeek in 1831. He is famous for his dignified pictures and statues of coal miners, steelworkers and dockers, and he lived in Brussels, where he died in 1905.

James Wilson Carmichael was an English painter born in Newcastle upon Tyne in 1799. He started as a sailor and became a well-known painter of ships, sea battles and harbor scenes, and moved to London. He died in Scarborough in 1868.

Theodoros Vryzakis was a Greek painter born in Thebes in 1814. He studied in Munich and became known for large paintings of the Greek War of Independence, which helped shape Greek national memory. He died in Munich in 1878.

Ambroise Louis Garneray was a French painter born in Paris in 1783. He went to sea as a boy, was a prisoner of the British during the Napoleonic wars, and later became a famous painter of ships and sea battles. He died in Paris in 1857.

Fritz von Dardel was a Swedish artist born in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, in 1817. He moved to Stockholm and became a court painter, also known for lively cartoons and sketches of events of his day. He died in Stockholm in 1901.

Baldassare Verazzi was an Italian painter born in Caprezzo in 1819. He lived in Milan and painted historical pictures related to the Italian struggle for independence, including the Five Days of Milan. He died in Lesa in 1886.

Isidor Popper was a German lithographer and cartoonist born in Hildesheim in 1816. He worked in Hamburg, where he made satirical prints, including some about the revolution of 1848. He died in Hamburg in 1884.

Vasily Timm was a Russian painter and illustrator born in Riga in 1820. He worked in Saint Petersburg, painted historical scenes and published an illustrated magazine, and later lived in Germany. He died in Berlin in 1895.

Georg Bleibtreu was a German painter born in Xanten in 1828. He lived in Berlin and became a leading painter of the Prussian wars of the 1860s and 1870s, depicting them in huge canvases. He died in Charlottenburg in 1892.
Wilhelm Camphausen was a German painter born in Düsseldorf in 1818. He specialized in battle and military scenes, painted the wars of Prussia, and lived in Düsseldorf, where he died in 1885.

Michele Gordigiani was an Italian painter born in Florence in 1835. He became a popular portrait painter, painting the English poet Robert Browning and Italian politicians such as Cavour. He lived in Florence and died there in 1909.

Gerolamo Induno was an Italian painter born in Milan in 1825. He fought for Italian independence in the 1840s and 1850s, joined Garibaldi and painted scenes of battles and ordinary people during the Risorgimento. He died in Milan in 1890.

Adolphe Yvon was a French painter born in Eschviller in 1817. He painted large battles for the French army, including the Crimean and Italian campaigns, and spent his life in Paris, where he died in 1893.

Carlo Bossoli was an Italian-Swiss painter born near Lugano in 1815. He worked in Odessa and then Turin, where he painted detailed pictures of the battles and events of the Italian wars of independence. He died in Turin in 1884.

Domenico Induno was an Italian painter born in Milan in 1815, the older brother of Gerolamo Induno. He painted scenes of everyday life and portraits of Risorgimento heroes. He lived in Milan and died there in 1878.

Franz von Lenbach was a German painter born in Schrobenhausen in 1836. He became the most fashionable portrait painter in Munich and was famous for his many portraits of Otto von Bismarck and of the pope and emperors. He died in Munich in 1904.
